recent_commits.message: Persist zip_peek() to disk and thread skip_on_api_limit through it (#427)
recent_commits.body:
zip_peek()'s result was cached only in memory (.zip_peek_cache), reset every
R process, unlike repo_info_cache() which already persists a repository's
LISTING to disk for exactly this reason. Added an on-disk cache
(R/zip-peek-cache.R, mirroring repo-info-cache.R's shape: one file per
archive URL, opt-in via cache = TRUE) and wired it into zip_peek(),
zip_decision(), .zip_fetch_members(), and .code_expand_zip(), plus all of
their call sites in repo_check.R, data_check.R, code_check.R, and
repo-download.R.

Also fixed skip_on_api_limit not reaching zip_peek()'s own HTTP helpers:
.head_size(), .http_range_get(), .http_range_tail(), .http_range_suffix(),
.http_range_bytes(), and .range_size() all called .wait_out_known_rate_limit()
and the retry factories with no skip_on_api_limit argument, so a confirmed
exhausted rate limit was always waited out during a zip peek regardless of
what the caller asked for -- the argument only reached them via the global
metacheck.skip_on_api_limit option. repo_check() had no skip_on_api_limit
parameter at all; added one, and data_check()/code_check() now forward their
own skip_on_api_limit both to repo_check() (via module_run()) and to the
zip-peeking step, matching how they already forward cache the same way.

recent_commits.message: Fix zip listing on S3-backed hosts (#424), install-loop variables as packages (#421), empty code files (#425)
recent_commits.body:
#424: zip_peek() on Dryad, Figshare and Harvard Dataverse
- These hosts redirect downloads to Amazon S3, which refuses HEAD (403)
  but honours ranged GETs. When HEAD gives no size, the tail is now
  requested by distance from the end ("bytes=-n") and the total read
  from Content-Range; a 416 answer is handled. The fallback reads the
  status before any body and accepts only 206, so a host that ignores
  the range cannot send a whole archive.
- A size is taken from HEAD only when the answer is 2xx; a 403 on a
  size request is no longer retried.
- .remote_size() falls back to a one-byte ranged GET the same way.
- Removed the OSF, Zenodo and Dataverse whole-archive routes in
  download_repo_files(): those archives never report a size, so the
  routes never ran. Removed .remote_content_length().
- Dryad, GitHub and GitLab archives now follow one rule: size estimated
  from listed file sizes, skipped when unknown or above 2x
  max_download_size, and stopped during download at 2x. GitHub and
  GitLab previously had no limit.
- osf_file_download(mode = "zip"): max_download_size is a budget for the
  whole project. A node whose archive does not fit is downloaded file by
  file within the budget (previously reported as "not downloaded" and
  then downloaded without limit). Partial archives are deleted.
- peek_zips now defaults to TRUE in data_check and reproducibility_check.

#421: dependency extraction
- code_library_names() no longer reports a variable's name as a package
  in install.packages(), requireNamespace(), or library()/require() with
  character.only = TRUE. Variables are resolved to the literal names
  assigned in the file (including for-loop variables, lapply(pkgs,
  library), p_load(char = pkgs)), and dropped otherwise.
- A package install.packages() cannot find is reported with its "not
  available" warning instead of "installed but not loadable".
- A 404 from the CRAN Archive is reported as "not found in the CRAN
  Archive", not as a network failure.

#425: empty code files
- code_abs_path(), code_setwd(), code_install_packages() and
  code_line_stats() handle an empty file without warnings or errors;
  code_parse_r() no longer reads the first line of an empty file.
  code_check previously recorded empty files as errored.

Tests
- New tests for all of the above.
- Existing tests: restore the real zip_peek() after tests that replace
  it; give new download tests their own repository names; add an
  renv.lock to the code_check green-light test (required since 9285b1f).

recent_commits.message: Convert Grobid TEI to bibr export schema 12.0
recent_commits.body:
grobid_to_bibr(schema_version = "12.0") converts Grobid TEI into a 12.x
paper and saves it as a 12.0 file:

- ids are 1-based positions in document order;
- xref targets come from the xml:id each <ref> points at, for bib,
  figure, table and foot references;
- each caption and footnote is one text row with no section, after the
  body and the reference list, and there are no pseudo-sections; a
  caption starts with its printed label, taken from <head> when figDesc
  leaves it out;
- the source is the PDF next to the TEI (published.pdf for
  published.pdf.tei.xml), else the TEI, so source.sha256 matches a bibr
  export of the same PDF; paper_id is the source's name without its
  extension;
- the producer is Grobid, with the version in the TEI header, and the
  converter is metacheck; completed_at is when Grobid extracted the
  content, from the same header, else the time of the conversion;
- metacheck's own warning codes start with METACHECK_.

The body sentences are made as before. Without schema_version, the
conversion is unchanged.
recent_commits.author: Jakub Werner

recent_commits.message: Write bibr export schema 12.0 with paper_write()
recent_commits.body:
paper_write(schema_version = "12.0") saves a paper read from a bibr 12.0
export as a 12.0 file. It keeps the paper's extraction block, so a bibr
export keeps bibr as its producer and bibr's completed_at, and names
metacheck as the converter: rewriting bibr's exports changes nothing but
converter. bib_match rows made by add_bib_match() are converted to the
12.0 columns, and a score that is not on the 0-1 scale is written as null
with a METACHECK_MATCH_SCORE_NOT_0_1 warning. A paper in the older format
is refused, and so is one read from a later 12.x, since its rewrite would
have to keep keys metacheck does not know. Without schema_version,
paper_write() writes what it wrote before.

The tests validate what they write against bibr's strict schema (a copy
in tests/testthat/fixtures/bibr12) when jsonvalidate, now in Suggests, is
installed.
recent_commits.author: Jakub Werner

recent_commits.message: Read bibr export schema 12.x files
recent_commits.body:
.read_bibr() now sends a file with a root schema_version (bibr export
schema 11 and later) to .read_bibr12(), which reads 12.x and stops on any
other version. Files without a root schema_version read exactly as
before. Keys that a later 12.x adds are ignored.

A 12.x paper keeps metacheck's info table, made from metadata and source,
and info_match (metadata_match); the other tables keep their 12.x names
and meanings. Captions and footnotes are text rows with no section that
figure, table and the new footnote table point at with text_id; xref_id
is the row's own key and target_id the row it cites; paper$extraction
holds the export's extraction block. Degrees of freedom stay in
parentheses, as metacheck's statistics code expects.

inst/schema/paper-bibr12.json lists the optional tables and columns this
adds. paper_validate() and .paper_coerce() merge it into paper.json and
skip properties that are not tables (extraction); paper() and paper.json
are unchanged. ref_consistency, ref_miscitation and the table captions of
match_reported_output() read 12.x papers, and ref_accuracy compares the
0-1 match scores of 12.x papers with suggest_score / 100.

recent_commits.message: Fix .reproducibility_check_batch() hang from callr pipe deadlock (#420)
recent_commits.body:
callr::r_bg() was launched with its default stdout = "|" / stderr = "|",
which pipes a worker's output through a small, fixed-size OS buffer.
Nothing in the polling loop drains those pipes while a worker is still
running, so a paper whose output exceeded the buffer before the parent
read it would block the child on its next write() forever. The process
stays alive (is_alive() == TRUE, CPU frozen rather than accumulating),
so its slot in `running` never frees, the queue never advances past it,
and the dispatcher hangs indefinitely with the remaining queued papers
never launched.

Redirect each worker's stdout/stderr to temp files instead, tracked in
new out_files/err_files lists keyed by pid (the callr process object is
a locked R6 environment and rejects new fields directly). The failure
path now reads the stderr file instead of p$read_all_error(), and both
temp files are removed once a worker's result has been collected.

Verified against a real Docker run (workers = 2, 3 papers): all papers
launch, finish, and combine correctly.

recent_commits.message: Fix capture_module_tables() saving modules unnamed (#419)
recent_commits.body:
collect_module_tables() looked up saved modules by name
(j$modules[[module]]), but capture_module_tables() never named the
outputs list, so the lookup always missed and the function silently
returned an empty data frame for every paper. .load_module_tables()
had the same problem via names(saved$modules).

stripped as plumbing), with a positional fallback for any NA/blank/
duplicate name. Also warn in collect_module_tables() when files exist
but none matched, instead of silently returning empty.

recent_commits.body:
DataONE: added data.piscoweb.org (PISCO, UC Santa Barbara) as a known
member node, and fixed .dataone_pid() not recognising a bare DOI whose
suffix itself contains a further slash (PISCO's own 10.6085/AA/<id>

domain in the URL at all, which dataone_links() could not resolve at
all before this fix.

Figshare: added 28 more institutional instances (found via DataCite's
client registry, searched for "figshare" in the client name) and
Monash University's bridges.monash.edu (found separately, via a real
paper citation, since its DataCite client is named "Monash University"
rather than mentioning Figshare). Taught .figshare_id()/figshare_links()
to recognise each instance's own DOI prefix (e.g. 10.26180 for Monash,
10.25375 for ZivaHub/UCT) when cited as a bare DOI with no host domain
in the URL -- previously only the generic 10.6084/m9.figshare.* DOI
shape was recognised this way, silently missing every institutional
instance's own prefix regardless of how many hosts were already in
.figshare_vanity_hosts(). Also anchored the new id-extraction pattern
on a non-digit boundary rather than end-of-string, since a trailing
sentence period from ordinary prose ("...19095317.v1.") is a common
real-extraction artifact that end-of-string anchoring silently missed.

Every added host confirmed live to answer Figshare's own single-page-app
shell (HTTP 202, non-JSON body) rather than a real API response, the
same discipline the existing 16 vanity hosts use; several DataCite-listed
candidates were checked and excluded because their real platform is
something else entirely (DataverseNO, DTU's Orbit repository, University
of Salford's Worktribe platform).

recent_commits.message: Fix systemic under-counting in the Dataverse DOI-prefix allowlist
recent_commits.body:
The allowlist added in the previous PR was built by sampling only the
first 25 DOIs DataCite's search returned per host, which missed every
additional prefix on any host with more real DOIs than that (63 of the
121 known hosts, some by orders of magnitude -- dataverse.harvard.edu
alone has 817,836 real DOIs and was missing its 10.26300 prefix
entirely).

Found when a paper citing 10.7939/DVN/M6Q2PE, the University of
Alberta's legacy Dataverse prefix (now migrated onto the shared
Borealis platform at borealisdata.ca), failed to resolve even though
borealisdata.ca was already a known host, mapped to only its dominant
prefix (10.5683).

Every host was re-queried using DataCite's facet aggregation
(disable-facets=false on the /dois search), which returns every
distinct prefix actually in use for a host, with its real count, in
one request instead of a sample. The allowlist now carries 100
distinct prefixes across the same 87 hosts (up from 87 prefixes).

recent_commits.body:
Dryad DOIs are not all issued under the 10.5061 prefix; found the
complete set of 14 real prefixes by exhaustively sampling DataCite's
DOI index, each individually confirmed live to resolve to a real
datadryad.org dataset page.

A bare DOI with no host domain in the URL (e.g. CIRAD Dataverse's
"https://doi.org/10.18167/DVN1/T0DMFJ") was invisible to
dataverse_links() even though the host itself is already known;
added a per-host, individually-verified DOI-prefix allowlist
covering 87 of 121 known Dataverse installations, found and verified
the same way as the Dryad prefixes.

While verifying both fixes against real papers, found that calling
<platform>_info() with the table <platform>_links() itself produced
(the normal, documented usage) crashes with a left_join column-name
collision whenever a repository isn't found -- confirmed in Dryad,
Dataverse, DataONE, Figshare, Mendeley Data, ReShare, and Zenodo.
Fixed by dropping the caller's pre-existing derived columns before
each function recomputes and joins its own.

Found while investigating disagreements in the Cooper et al.
validation corpus flagged as repo_check misses that were actually
real, working repository citations.

recent_commits.message: Fix `debit_plot()` and plot argument handling
recent_commits.body:
* `debit_plot()` recycled the `n` column along a single DEBIT line; it
  now draws the line for the correct `n`. If `n` varies, it draws the
  lines for the smallest and largest `n` and shades the band between
  them, which contains all the others. `NA` rows are dropped with a
  warning, and it returns its plot rather than printing it.
* `debit_plot()` no longer draws outer boxes around the rectangles;
  `show_outer_boxes` and the `tile_*` arguments are gone. Each rectangle
  is drawn over a point at the reported mean and SD instead, so that it
  shows up even when it is too small to see.
* `grim_plot(n = ...)` now ends the x-axis at `n`, and
  `split_by_digits = TRUE` always returns a list.
* `grim_plot_values()` and `grimmer_plot_values()` reject invalid input
  with clear errors.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Fix duplicate counts and audit summary statistics
recent_commits.body:
* `audit()` of `duplicate_detect()` output dropped columns without
  duplicates, which also skewed `.total`.
* `duplicate_count_colpair()`'s `rate_y` could exceed 1.
* `audit_summary_stats()` computed `na_rate` for `.total` over rows, not
  values, and gave `Inf`/`-Inf` for all-`NA` columns.
* `duplicate_count()` now uses a named vector's names as `locations`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Split parenthesized strings one at a time
recent_commits.body:
* The split pieces were pooled and re-chunked by their average count, so
one cell with an extra pair of parentheses shifted every later value
into the wrong row. Separators are now matched literally, `NA` no
longer breaks `split_by_parens()`, and `transform = TRUE` no longer
mixes up columns such as `exp_sd`. `row_to_colnames()` handles `NA`
header cells.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Fix decimal counting, `restore_zeros()`, and rounding input checks
recent_commits.body:
* `sep` is matched literally, as documented; the default is now `"."`.
* `decimal_places()` and `decimal_places_scalar()` agree on malformed
  strings and read `"inf"`/`"nan"` in any case.
* `restore_zeros()` handled scientific notation and wide padding badly.
* `reround()` and `unround()` validate `digits` alike; `unround()`
  treats an infinite `x` as missing.
* `rounding_bias()`, the `round_*()` functions, and
  `reround_to_fraction()` handle strings, `symmetric`, recycling, and
  `NA` properly.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Fix sequence, dispersion, and total-n edge cases
recent_commits.body:

recent_commits.body:
The narrowed note-distance rule (previous commit) rejects a distant "note" only
when running prose lies between it and the table. On 10.48550/arxiv.2410.21901
p7 the gap between Table 6 and the Figure 5 caption is the figure itself, which
carries no text. So the caption came back as Table 6's note, the region ran
into it, and Table 6 reverted to fused label/value cells ("H:7,V:11 94.83").

A band of more than 40pt with no upright text inside the table's x-range now
disqualifies the gap too. Consecutive table rows sit 10-14pt apart, and a band
that tall with nothing in it is a figure or empty page. Re-extracting the 11
papers whose regions moved restores Table 6 to 10x4 with every value in its own
cell. cmaj.230841 and 00221465251343322 keep their real notes.

recent_commits.message: fix(tables): two region guards narrowed after a firing census and a cross-model review
recent_commits.body:
Measured every firing of the new detect.py guards over the 102-paper manifest
and judged each against the text it acted on. Two guards were wrong some of the
time. Both are now narrowed.

- The lone-rule filter dropped a table's OWN unique top rule:
  10.1038/s41598-023-50460-2 p4 Table 3 draws one full-width rule
  (x 159.4->552.2) above shorter recurring rules. 1 of 9 firings, confirmed on
  the rasterized page. Sol and Sonnet each raised the same shape independently
  in the consult round, and Sonnet reproduced it on constructed rules. Every
  correct firing dropped a rule BELOW the table (a footer separator, the next
  table's top rule), so only such a rule is now dropped. Final: 5 firings,
  5/5 correct.
- The note-distance rule assumed a ruled table's last detected rule is its
  last row. On 10.1503/cmaj.230841 p6 and 10.1177/00221465251343322 p7 the
  table continues far below the rules found, and the rejected "Note:" /
  "Source:" line was the table's real note. That was 2 of 32 firings; final
  output was unchanged in both, but the premise was false. A distant note is
  now rejected only when a running-prose line (spanning at least 60% of the
  column, no gap of 12pt or more, at least 25 glyphs) lies between the table
  and the note. Final: 21 firings, 21/21 correct (page footers, section
  headings, a figure caption, citation superscripts, a URL footnote).

The caption locator was 12/12 correct and is unchanged. Sonnet's
justified-stretch case (a word space of 6pt or more before a cross-reference)
is documented at the threshold as a known, bounded limit: it falls back to the
pre-v2.4.145 choice.

Each narrowing was mutation-tested: removing it turns exactly its new unit
test red.

recent_commits.message: fix(extract): retire the U+FFFD recovery -- it could substitute a wrong statistic
recent_commits.body:
Owner decision 2026-09-24. When pdftotext emitted three or more U+FFFD, extract_pdf
ran pdfplumber over the whole document and then either REPLACED the entire text
(Mode A) or patched words one at a time from a global token set (Mode B). Every
load-bearing claim against it was reproduced by running the code:

  * Mode A's guard, _reading_order_agrees, returned True for a document's exact
    REVERSE (under 2000 chars it checks length only), for its blocks SHUFFLED
    (it tests substring membership, never order), and for completely UNRELATED
    text (when no clean 60-char window exists it skips all three checks and
    returns True vacuously).
  * Mode A joined pages with "\n\n" instead of form feeds, so every downstream
    page boundary collapsed to page 1.
  * Mode B turned `partial <U+FFFD>2 = .35` into `partial R2 = .35` -- a partial
    eta-squared relabelled as an R-squared -- because "unique" meant unique among
    distinct token spellings anywhere in the document, and the SMP Greek it
    looked up had already been spelled out, so the true `eta2` could never match.
  * Mode B is not dormant: on vancouver/plos_med_1.pdf (9 U+FFFD) it EXECUTED on
    the live document and returned 0 patches only because no word had a unique
    look-alike.
  * Across all 102 corpus papers neither mode was ever accepted.

A visible U+FFFD is a flag a consumer can act on; a plausible wrong token is not.
Removed: the recovery block and every helper that served only it
(_patch_fffds_word_by_word, _reading_order_agrees, _build_smp_greek /
_SMP_GREEK_TO_ASCII, _smp_to_ascii_map, _recover_with_pdfplumber). Nothing
correctly encoded is lost: normalize.py maps SMP math-italic characters that
pdftotext DOES decode (_MATH_ALNUM_RE), and the removed Greek table was the
second copy that the ONE-CONCEPT-ONE-TABLE rule was written about.

Tests: the eight word-patch unit tests and test_smp_greek_agrees_with_a5.py (all
five of its tests exercised only the removed table) are gone. The strict xfail
test_nature_smp_recovery, whose premise had been false since 2026-09-17, is
replaced by test_replacement_characters_pass_through_as_printed on the one corpus
paper that carries U+FFFD. Mutation-checked: making extract_pdf rewrite U+FFFD
turns it red ("found 0"). The compat allowlist no longer accepts a method value
that cannot be produced. Docs, README, SYMBOL_CONTRACT and DESIGN updated; the
DESIGN section is kept and marked retired.

CONSUMER-VISIBLE:
  method   before: "pdftotext_default+pdfplumber_recovery" / "...+pdfplumber_word_patch"
           after:  never produced
  text     before: on >= 3 U+FFFD, possibly a different document's worth of text
           after:  U+FFFD passed through as printed
  fallbacks: "pdfplumber_recovery_exception" no longer emitted
No corpus paper's output changes; the change bites only outside the corpus.

_new_commits.message: fix(tables): two region guards narrowed after a firing census and a cross-model review
_new_commits.body:
Measured every firing of the new detect.py guards over the 102-paper manifest
and judged each against the text it acted on. Two guards were wrong some of the
time. Both are now narrowed.

- The lone-rule filter dropped a table's OWN unique top rule:
  10.1038/s41598-023-50460-2 p4 Table 3 draws one full-width rule
  (x 159.4->552.2) above shorter recurring rules. 1 of 9 firings, confirmed on
  the rasterized page. Sol and Sonnet each raised the same shape independently
  in the consult round, and Sonnet reproduced it on constructed rules. Every
  correct firing dropped a rule BELOW the table (a footer separator, the next
  table's top rule), so only such a rule is now dropped. Final: 5 firings,
  5/5 correct.
- The note-distance rule assumed a ruled table's last detected rule is its
  last row. On 10.1503/cmaj.230841 p6 and 10.1177/00221465251343322 p7 the
  table continues far below the rules found, and the rejected "Note:" /
  "Source:" line was the table's real note. That was 2 of 32 firings; final
  output was unchanged in both, but the premise was false. A distant note is
  now rejected only when a running-prose line (spanning at least 60% of the
  column, no gap of 12pt or more, at least 25 glyphs) lies between the table
  and the note. Final: 21 firings, 21/21 correct (page footers, section
  headings, a figure caption, citation superscripts, a URL footnote).

The caption locator was 12/12 correct and is unchanged. Sonnet's
justified-stretch case (a word space of 6pt or more before a cross-reference)
is documented at the threshold as a known, bounded limit: it falls back to the
pre-v2.4.145 choice.

Each narrowing was mutation-tested: removing it turns exactly its new unit
test red.

_new_commits.message: fix(tables): read Nature `N |` captions, and keep uncaptioned grids labelled instead of dropping them
_new_commits.body:
Two defects, found together on nature/nat_comms_1.pdf, owner-directed 2026-09-24
("investigate, understand what happened and fix ... best to retain information and
not drop. if unsure what that is - we keep but label it accordingly").

1. THE PIPE. The Nature family prints `Fig. 1 | Title` / `Table 1 | Title`. FOUR
   caption patterns required `.`/`:` (or a space and a capital) after the number,
   so every caption in that house style was invisible -- figures and tables alike.
   All four now build from ONE `CAPTION_PIPE_SEPARATOR` in tables/captions.py
   (captions.py x2, camelot_extract.py's caption-row and caption-number patterns);
   before, the second pair never learned the pipe, so the caption line stayed inside
   the grid as the table's first cell. A test asserts the four agree.
   Census, all 102 corpus papers: +29 caption matches in 5 papers, all Nature
   Communications, 29/29 real captions. End to end on nat_comms_1..5, same base,
   only the pattern differing: figures 0->5, 0->4, 0->6, 0->3, 0->5; tables +1
   (nat_comms_2), +4 (nat_comms_4), +1 (nat_comms_5), with real cells.

2. THE SILENT DROP. extract_structured discarded every Camelot grid on a page with
   no detected caption (and every grid no caption matched) with a bare `continue`:
   no event, no count, justified as "rare in the APA corpus" -- never measured.
   Such grids are now KEPT with the new field caption_status="uncaptioned_candidate"
   (label/caption None, id `u<n>`), counted as camelot_table_kept_without_caption,
   and rendered in their own "Uncaptioned table candidates (unverified)" section --
   never anchored inline, where an empty label would search for the bare word
   "Table". A grid overlapping a kept table on the same page (>= 50% of the smaller
   box) is a surviving copy and is deduplicated, recorded as such. Every Table now
   carries caption_status: matched / none_found (DOCX: the file declares the table)
   / uncaptioned_candidate.
   Corpus sweep: 83 of 102 papers gain >= 1 candidate, 369 in total, 40 deduped. A
   random sample is roughly half REAL statistical tables that were being thrown away
   (a regression table "Coeff. (SE)", "Odds ratio with 95%...", a 220-cell JAMA table)
   and half furniture (running headers, title blocks, figure internals) -- which is
   exactly why the label says "unverified", not "table".

THE FIXTURES WERE ON THE WRONG PAPERS. nature_minimal_rule ("minimal-rule tables,
gray-band header") pointed at nat_comms_1, which prints no table; nat_comms_figure_only
("figures, no tables") pointed at nat_comms_2, which prints a gray-band Table 1.
Verified by rasterizing both. Swapped, counts set from the printed pages (1 table /
4 figures; 0 / 5), and the sha256 text pins moved with their papers.

Gates that could only pass, now able to fail:
- smoke figure count: +/-6 tolerance accepted ZERO figures (two Nature fixtures
  extracted 0 while printing 4 and 5); zero is now its own assertion. The table count
  compares CAPTIONED tables, since candidates are extra by construction.
- four figure tests did pytest.skip("no figures detected") -- which is how zero
  figures stayed invisible. Now assertions. Two of them test figures/detect.find_figures,
  which has NO production caller and fails on this paper because pdfplumber collapsed
  every space in its layout text ("Fig.1|Lethaleffects..."): strict xfail, reason
  recorded, goes red the day that module works.
- test_wrapped_contact_strip: the contact block must stay out of the BODY (its name);
  it may now appear, labelled, in the candidates section. Scoped to the body.
- table ids may start `u`.

Two-sided: tests/test_nature_pipe_captions_real_pdf.py restores the old pattern and
requires the figures to vanish; the keep-and-label test was mutation-checked by
restoring the silent drop in-process -> "grids on this paper were dropped again".

CONSUMER-VISIBLE: every Table gains `caption_status`; Nature-family papers gain
figures and tables; 83/102 corpus papers gain uncaptioned candidates in `tables` and a
new appendix section in rendered Markdown. TABLE_EXTRACTION_VERSION left to the
release coordinator (one bump with the concurrent table-region fix).

NOT fixed, newly exposed, handed on: nat_comms_4 Table 4 is printed ROTATED and is
captured as caption-only with raw_text "Article" (the running header); JAMA's
unnumbered "Table." caption is another caption gap.

Targeted: 91 passed, 2 xfailed (then the caption-text assertion corrected: 5/5).
_new_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

_new_commits.message: fix(tables): a wider table region stops at its own table, not the page furniture
_new_commits.body:
2c8b0dd (v2.4.143) widened caption-anchored regions so wide tables stopped
losing columns. That is kept. But four detectors were never written for a wide
region, and a 102-paper diff (v2.4.142 vs 2.4.144) found real tables they
emptied or garbled. Every change is keyed on what the file states:

- `_bbox_of_caption_line` matched by CONTAINMENT, so a body sentence
  "presented in Table 4." above the real "TABLE 4" heading won
  (10.5465/amj.2016.1196 p19). A row whose match starts a text block (the first
  glyph, or after a gap of 6pt or more) is now preferred. With none, the old
  first-containing row is returned.
- `_widen_to_left_aligned_rows` buckets words by y across the WHOLE page, so a
  row "starting at the left edge" carried a side-note column
  (10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2023.48333 p6: the Model 1/Model 2 hazard ratios
  came out interleaved glyph by glyph) and a rotated copyright strip
  (10.1136/bmjopen-2022-066361 p6). It now runs only for a whitespace run (a
  ruled table's rules state its width) and skips non-upright words.
- the lattice union admitted a lone page-footer rule (x 47.9->562.8 beside
  eight table rules at 47.9->395.1). A rule that is the only one of its width,
  AND reaches beyond the recurring rules' extent, is dropped from the union.
- `_detect_footnote_below` took the first small text anywhere below a table:
  the rotated strip (bmjopen: Table 4 shipped with 0 rows), the page footer
  440pt below (10.48550/arxiv.2410.21901 Table 5, EMPTY), and a figure caption
  (its Table 6, EMPTY). Non-upright glyphs are excluded. For a ruled table,
  whose last rule is its last row, a note must start within one note-row gap
  (25pt) of it.

The note-distance rule was first applied to every signal. A geometry-only
census (all 429 captions, HEAD vs this) showed it moving 112 regions in 43
papers, and 10.1525/collabra.90203 Table 7 would have lost its lower 300pt.
Scoped to lattice, it moves 63 regions in 31 papers. A full
extract_pdf_structured diff over the 39 affected papers changes 15; each
changed table was checked against the printed page. No printed value is lost.
Recovered: jama_open_2 T2, bmj_open_1 T4 (now all 6 columns),
arxiv.2410.21901 T5/T6. Newly captured: 10.1016/j.jesp.2021.104154 T3.
Corrected: 10.1017/jdm.2023.15 T3 had carried Table 2's descriptives while the
regression table reached nothing.

NOT recovered: 10.5465/amj.2016.1196 Table 4, lost from v2.4.143 on. v2.4.142's
partial copy (M, SD only) existed only because of the mis-located caption. With
the caption now right, the table (rules drawn as rectangles, a lower-triangular
correlation matrix) is found by no detector. Reported, not hidden.

Two docstrings stated safety claims this disproved; corrected in place.
LESSONS L-060.

The run of appended rows now stops at the top edge of another same-page ruled
table sharing its x-range, or at a `Table N.` / `Figure N.` caption row. The box

_new_commits.message: fix(extract): retire the U+FFFD recovery -- it could substitute a wrong statistic
_new_commits.body:
Owner decision 2026-09-24. When pdftotext emitted three or more U+FFFD, extract_pdf
ran pdfplumber over the whole document and then either REPLACED the entire text
(Mode A) or patched words one at a time from a global token set (Mode B). Every
load-bearing claim against it was reproduced by running the code:

  * Mode A's guard, _reading_order_agrees, returned True for a document's exact
    REVERSE (under 2000 chars it checks length only), for its blocks SHUFFLED
    (it tests substring membership, never order), and for completely UNRELATED
    text (when no clean 60-char window exists it skips all three checks and
    returns True vacuously).
  * Mode A joined pages with "\n\n" instead of form feeds, so every downstream
    page boundary collapsed to page 1.
  * Mode B turned `partial <U+FFFD>2 = .35` into `partial R2 = .35` -- a partial
    eta-squared relabelled as an R-squared -- because "unique" meant unique among
    distinct token spellings anywhere in the document, and the SMP Greek it
    looked up had already been spelled out, so the true `eta2` could never match.
  * Mode B is not dormant: on vancouver/plos_med_1.pdf (9 U+FFFD) it EXECUTED on
    the live document and returned 0 patches only because no word had a unique
    look-alike.
  * Across all 102 corpus papers neither mode was ever accepted.

A visible U+FFFD is a flag a consumer can act on; a plausible wrong token is not.
Removed: the recovery block and every helper that served only it
(_patch_fffds_word_by_word, _reading_order_agrees, _build_smp_greek /
_SMP_GREEK_TO_ASCII, _smp_to_ascii_map, _recover_with_pdfplumber). Nothing
correctly encoded is lost: normalize.py maps SMP math-italic characters that
pdftotext DOES decode (_MATH_ALNUM_RE), and the removed Greek table was the
second copy that the ONE-CONCEPT-ONE-TABLE rule was written about.

Tests: the eight word-patch unit tests and test_smp_greek_agrees_with_a5.py (all
five of its tests exercised only the removed table) are gone. The strict xfail
test_nature_smp_recovery, whose premise had been false since 2026-09-17, is
replaced by test_replacement_characters_pass_through_as_printed on the one corpus
paper that carries U+FFFD. Mutation-checked: making extract_pdf rewrite U+FFFD
turns it red ("found 0"). The compat allowlist no longer accepts a method value
that cannot be produced. Docs, README, SYMBOL_CONTRACT and DESIGN updated; the
DESIGN section is kept and marked retired.

CONSUMER-VISIBLE:
  method   before: "pdftotext_default+pdfplumber_recovery" / "...+pdfplumber_word_patch"
           after:  never produced
  text     before: on >= 3 U+FFFD, possibly a different document's worth of text
           after:  U+FFFD passed through as printed
  fallbacks: "pdfplumber_recovery_exception" no longer emitted
No corpus paper's output changes; the change bites only outside the corpus.

python -m pytest tests/test_extraction.py tests/test_v23_1_fixes.py
  tests/test_v2_backwards_compat.py tests/test_mathitalic_greek_real_pdf.py
  tests/test_symbol_contract.py tests/test_public_repo_hygiene.py -n 4
  -> 162 passed

* feat(llm): support openai/gpt-5.6-sol-pro on the direct OpenAI route (#1)

The -pro suffix is an OpenRouter-only variant ID; OpenAI's own API 404s
on it. With a direct OPENAI_API_KEY, LLMClient now rewrites the wire
request to the real model gpt-5.6-sol plus a reasoning {"mode": "pro"}
body via the new DIRECT_REQUEST_MODEL_ALIASES table in models.py, and
suppresses the conflicting default reasoning_effort. The OpenRouter
route keeps sending the variant ID untouched. The variant's pricing and
272k long-context tier are registered (identical to base Sol per
OpenRouter, verified 2026-08-30) so the pre-flight cost gate no longer
quotes $0.

Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

highlights.message: Persist zip_peek() to disk and thread skip_on_api_limit through it (#427)
highlights.body:
zip_peek()'s result was cached only in memory (.zip_peek_cache), reset every
R process, unlike repo_info_cache() which already persists a repository's
LISTING to disk for exactly this reason. Added an on-disk cache
(R/zip-peek-cache.R, mirroring repo-info-cache.R's shape: one file per
archive URL, opt-in via cache = TRUE) and wired it into zip_peek(),
zip_decision(), .zip_fetch_members(), and .code_expand_zip(), plus all of
their call sites in repo_check.R, data_check.R, code_check.R, and
repo-download.R.

Also fixed skip_on_api_limit not reaching zip_peek()'s own HTTP helpers:
.head_size(), .http_range_get(), .http_range_tail(), .http_range_suffix(),
.http_range_bytes(), and .range_size() all called .wait_out_known_rate_limit()
and the retry factories with no skip_on_api_limit argument, so a confirmed
exhausted rate limit was always waited out during a zip peek regardless of
what the caller asked for -- the argument only reached them via the global
metacheck.skip_on_api_limit option. repo_check() had no skip_on_api_limit
parameter at all; added one, and data_check()/code_check() now forward their
own skip_on_api_limit both to repo_check() (via module_run()) and to the
zip-peeking step, matching how they already forward cache the same way.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

highlights.message: Merge pull request #426 from scienceverse/fix-424-zip-peek-s3
highlights.body: Fix zip listing on S3-backed hosts, install-loop variables as packages, empty code files
highlights.author: Daniel Lakens

highlights.message: Fix zip listing on S3-backed hosts (#424), install-loop variables as packages (#421), empty code files (#425)
highlights.body:
#424: zip_peek() on Dryad, Figshare and Harvard Dataverse
- These hosts redirect downloads to Amazon S3, which refuses HEAD (403)
  but honours ranged GETs. When HEAD gives no size, the tail is now
  requested by distance from the end ("bytes=-n") and the total read
  from Content-Range; a 416 answer is handled. The fallback reads the
  status before any body and accepts only 206, so a host that ignores
  the range cannot send a whole archive.
- A size is taken from HEAD only when the answer is 2xx; a 403 on a
  size request is no longer retried.
- .remote_size() falls back to a one-byte ranged GET the same way.
- Removed the OSF, Zenodo and Dataverse whole-archive routes in
  download_repo_files(): those archives never report a size, so the
  routes never ran. Removed .remote_content_length().
- Dryad, GitHub and GitLab archives now follow one rule: size estimated
  from listed file sizes, skipped when unknown or above 2x
  max_download_size, and stopped during download at 2x. GitHub and
  GitLab previously had no limit.
- osf_file_download(mode = "zip"): max_download_size is a budget for the
  whole project. A node whose archive does not fit is downloaded file by
  file within the budget (previously reported as "not downloaded" and
  then downloaded without limit). Partial archives are deleted.
- peek_zips now defaults to TRUE in data_check and reproducibility_check.

#421: dependency extraction
- code_library_names() no longer reports a variable's name as a package
  in install.packages(), requireNamespace(), or library()/require() with
  character.only = TRUE. Variables are resolved to the literal names
  assigned in the file (including for-loop variables, lapply(pkgs,
  library), p_load(char = pkgs)), and dropped otherwise.
- A package install.packages() cannot find is reported with its "not
  available" warning instead of "installed but not loadable".
- A 404 from the CRAN Archive is reported as "not found in the CRAN
  Archive", not as a network failure.

#425: empty code files
- code_abs_path(), code_setwd(), code_install_packages() and
  code_line_stats() handle an empty file without warnings or errors;
  code_parse_r() no longer reads the first line of an empty file.
  code_check previously recorded empty files as errored.

Tests
- New tests for all of the above.
- Existing tests: restore the real zip_peek() after tests that replace
  it; give new download tests their own repository names; add an
  renv.lock to the code_check green-light test (required since 9285b1f).
highlights.author: Lakens

highlights.message: Fix `debit_plot()` and plot argument handling
highlights.body:
* `debit_plot()` recycled the `n` column along a single DEBIT line; it
  now draws the line for the correct `n`. If `n` varies, it draws the
  lines for the smallest and largest `n` and shades the band between
  them, which contains all the others. `NA` rows are dropped with a
  warning, and it returns its plot rather than printing it.
* `debit_plot()` no longer draws outer boxes around the rectangles;
  `show_outer_boxes` and the `tile_*` arguments are gone. Each rectangle
  is drawn over a point at the reported mean and SD instead, so that it
  shows up even when it is too small to see.
* `grim_plot(n = ...)` now ends the x-axis at `n`, and
  `split_by_digits = TRUE` always returns a list.
* `grim_plot_values()` and `grimmer_plot_values()` reject invalid input
  with clear errors.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Fix duplicate counts and audit summary statistics
highlights.body:
* `audit()` of `duplicate_detect()` output dropped columns without
  duplicates, which also skewed `.total`.
* `duplicate_count_colpair()`'s `rate_y` could exceed 1.
* `audit_summary_stats()` computed `na_rate` for `.total` over rows, not
  values, and gave `Inf`/`-Inf` for all-`NA` columns.
* `duplicate_count()` now uses a named vector's names as `locations`.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Split parenthesized strings one at a time
highlights.body:
* The split pieces were pooled and re-chunked by their average count, so
one cell with an extra pair of parentheses shifted every later value
into the wrong row. Separators are now matched literally, `NA` no
longer breaks `split_by_parens()`, and `transform = TRUE` no longer
mixes up columns such as `exp_sd`. `row_to_colnames()` handles `NA`
header cells.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Fix decimal counting, `restore_zeros()`, and rounding input checks
highlights.body:
* `sep` is matched literally, as documented; the default is now `"."`.
* `decimal_places()` and `decimal_places_scalar()` agree on malformed
  strings and read `"inf"`/`"nan"` in any case.
* `restore_zeros()` handled scientific notation and wide padding badly.
* `reround()` and `unround()` validate `digits` alike; `unround()`
  treats an infinite `x` as missing.
* `rounding_bias()`, the `round_*()` functions, and
  `reround_to_fraction()` handle strings, `symmetric`, recycling, and
  `NA` properly.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: test: correspondence-shaped files must live in communications/
highlights.body:
A gitignored prompt file sat in docs/ rather than communications/, where the
one-directory rule puts all correspondence. Git-scoped checks cannot see a
gitignored file, so this test scans the working tree itself (repo root and
docs/). Red with the file back in docs/, green after the move.

highlights.message: docs: two public tables still named the retired U+FFFD recovery as live
highlights.body:
docs/DESIGN.md's dependency table gave pdfplumber's purpose as "PDF SMP
Unicode recovery" and docs/BENCHMARKS.md named "pdfplumber recovery" as the
active handling step, although 2.4.145 retires that recovery. Both now say it
is retired. A test fails on any docs/*.md line that names the mechanism
without saying so (red on the pre-fix wording). The edited BENCHMARKS row also
named a private repository as its source; it now says what the corpus is.
highlights.author: Gilad Feldman

highlights.message: chore(harness): re-baseline Tier-D at the 2.4.145 candidate after a zero-regression A/B
highlights.body:
Whole-corpus A/B, arms run serially (v2.4.144 worktree vs this tree, same app
service at 46e9734, identity proven by each arm's /_diag render path): 0
regressions, 5 table_parity cells fixed, 21 known failures unchanged. Verdict
diff against the previous baseline is exactly those 5 fail->pass; every other
line is a new detail field. Text changed in 3 of 135 documents, each expected
(a duplicated page digit removed twice, one reference list reordered).
CHANGELOG gains the render-fix and harness-check entries and the measured
candidate counts.
highlights.author: Gilad Feldman

highlights.message: fix(harness): table_parity matches uncaptioned candidates to their own heading
highlights.body:
2.4.145 renders a kept uncaptioned grid under "### Uncaptioned candidate",
never "### Table N". The check compared Table headings against ALL tables, so
every paper with a candidate failed: 208 cells in the whole-corpus run, and
every one was explained exactly by the candidate count. Each class is now
counted against its own heading, so a candidate can neither pad the captioned
count nor hide a missing captioned table. With the noise gone the check shows
the one real defect underneath it: candidate <table> blocks the render chain
deletes (8 papers).
highlights.author: Gilad Feldman

highlights.message: Fix sequence, dispersion, and total-n edge cases
highlights.body:
* `reverse_map_total_n()` rebuilt the wrong total `n` unless
  `dispersion` started at 0.
* `seq_endpoint()` and `seq_distance()` drifted off the decimal level.
* `is_seq_linear()` accepted zigzags; the other predicates returned `NA`
  where the known values ruled a sequence out.
* `seq_disperse()` accepted a fractional `dispersion` and compared
  string limits as strings.
* `disperse_total()` and the total-n mappers crashed when no pair of
  group sizes was left, for a total below 2, and for 0-row data.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Make the GRIM probability exact for every rounding method
highlights.body:
* `(10^D - N * L) / 10^D` only holds for rounding methods with a single
half-open range one step wide. `"up_or_down"` admits ties toward both
neighbors, and `"ceiling_or_floor"` a range two steps wide.
`grim_probability()` and `grim_total()` now take `rounding` and
`threshold` and count exactly the values `grim()` rules out, and return
`NA` where `grim()` does. `grim_map()` passes its `rounding` on.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Close gaps in the tests' handling of untestable input
highlights.body:
* `grimmer()` checked the scale bounds before `n`, turning undecidable
  cases into `FALSE`. A negative `sd` is now `FALSE` with its own reason.
* `grim_values()` and `grim_closest()` skipped the decidability check.
* `grim_binomial()` and `grim_binomial_power()` crashed R on empty
  input inside poibin.
* A string `n` and an infinite `digits_*` now get clear errors.
* The missing-`digits_sd` error suggested a call that itself failed.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Anchor the patterns of `is_map_df()` and friends
highlights.body:
* `(^scrutiny_)*` made the prefix optional, so any class ending in `_map`
matched, and `is_map_basic_df()` rejected mappers with `map` in their
test name.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Read key arguments by value in `absorb_key_args()`
highlights.body:
* It parsed the unevaluated call, which through `lapply()` or
`purrr::map()` is `FUN(X[[i]], ...)`, and from a wrapper names a
variable rather than the column. It also silently ignored a key argument
whenever `data` already had a column of that name. The values are now
captured in the mapper's frame, and such a clash is an error.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Fix `items` and `case` in `*_map_seq()` output
highlights.body:
* The sequence mappers re-tested `n * items` with `items = 1`. GRIMMER
  needs `n` and `items` separately, so `grimmer_map_seq()` gave wrong
  verdicts, even for the reported values. `function_map()` now records
  which key column each helper is merged into, and `function_map_seq()`
  undoes the merge: `n` is dispersed as the sample size and `items` is
  returned as a column, which `audit_seq()` also reads.
* `case` is now the row number in the input data, not the position
  among the inconsistent rows, so results can be joined back.
* `audit_seq()` now accepts output from a single-step `dispersion`.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Write `expect_na()` with `pass()` and `fail()`
highlights.body:
* testthat 3.3.0 checks the inputs of `expect()`, which b5b2f3f worked
around on main. Now using the documented pattern for custom expectations
instead: https://testthat.r-lib.org/articles/custom-expectation.html
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Test that both `seq_disperse()` limits apply to both sides
highlights.body:
The fix went into edaada3; these are its tests, plus the corrected
expectations in `test-reverse-map-seq.R` that follow from it.

highlights.message: fix(render): the phantom-table stripper no longer deletes kept uncaptioned candidates

highlights.message: test(rule-40): two-sided gates for the four unasserted *_failed tokens

highlights.body:
The narrowed note-distance rule (previous commit) rejects a distant "note" only
when running prose lies between it and the table. On 10.48550/arxiv.2410.21901
p7 the gap between Table 6 and the Figure 5 caption is the figure itself, which
carries no text. So the caption came back as Table 6's note, the region ran

A band of more than 40pt with no upright text inside the table's x-range now
disqualifies the gap too. Consecutive table rows sit 10-14pt apart, and a band
that tall with nothing in it is a figure or empty page. Re-extracting the 11
papers whose regions moved restores Table 6 to 10x4 with every value in its own

highlights.body:

and judged each against the text it acted on. Two guards were wrong some of the
time. Both are now narrowed.

- The lone-rule filter dropped a table's OWN unique top rule:
  10.1038/s41598-023-50460-2 p4 Table 3 draws one full-width rule

  correct firing dropped a rule BELOW the table (a footer separator, the next

1. THE PIPE. The Nature family prints `Fig. 1 | Title` / `Table 1 | Title`. FOUR
   caption patterns required `.`/`:` (or a space and a capital) after the number,
   so every caption in that house style was invisible -- figures and tables alike.
   All four now build from ONE `CAPTION_PIPE_SEPARATOR` in tables/captions.py

highlights.message: fix(extract): retire the U+FFFD recovery -- it could substitute a wrong statistic
highlights.body:
Owner decision 2026-09-24. When pdftotext emitted three or more U+FFFD, extract_pdf
ran pdfplumber over the whole document and then either REPLACED the entire text
(Mode A) or patched words one at a time from a global token set (Mode B). Every
load-bearing claim against it was reproduced by running the code:

  * Mode A's guard, _reading_order_agrees, returned True for a document's exact
    REVERSE (under 2000 chars it checks length only), for its blocks SHUFFLED
    (it tests substring membership, never order), and for completely UNRELATED
    text (when no clean 60-char window exists it skips all three checks and
    returns True vacuously).
  * Mode A joined pages with "\n\n" instead of form feeds, so every downstream
    page boundary collapsed to page 1.
  * Mode B turned `partial <U+FFFD>2 = .35` into `partial R2 = .35` -- a partial
    eta-squared relabelled as an R-squared -- because "unique" meant unique among
    distinct token spellings anywhere in the document, and the SMP Greek it
    looked up had already been spelled out, so the true `eta2` could never match.
  * Mode B is not dormant: on vancouver/plos_med_1.pdf (9 U+FFFD) it EXECUTED on
    the live document and returned 0 patches only because no word had a unique
    look-alike.
  * Across all 102 corpus papers neither mode was ever accepted.

A visible U+FFFD is a flag a consumer can act on; a plausible wrong token is not.
Removed: the recovery block and every helper that served only it
(_patch_fffds_word_by_word, _reading_order_agrees, _build_smp_greek /
_SMP_GREEK_TO_ASCII, _smp_to_ascii_map, _recover_with_pdfplumber). Nothing
correctly encoded is lost: normalize.py maps SMP math-italic characters that
pdftotext DOES decode (_MATH_ALNUM_RE), and the removed Greek table was the
second copy that the ONE-CONCEPT-ONE-TABLE rule was written about.

Tests: the eight word-patch unit tests and test_smp_greek_agrees_with_a5.py (all
five of its tests exercised only the removed table) are gone. The strict xfail
test_nature_smp_recovery, whose premise had been false since 2026-09-17, is
replaced by test_replacement_characters_pass_through_as_printed on the one corpus
paper that carries U+FFFD. Mutation-checked: making extract_pdf rewrite U+FFFD
turns it red ("found 0"). The compat allowlist no longer accepts a method value
that cannot be produced. Docs, README, SYMBOL_CONTRACT and DESIGN updated; the
DESIGN section is kept and marked retired.

CONSUMER-VISIBLE:
  method   before: "pdftotext_default+pdfplumber_recovery" / "...+pdfplumber_word_patch"
           after:  never produced
  text     before: on >= 3 U+FFFD, possibly a different document's worth of text
           after:  U+FFFD passed through as printed
  fallbacks: "pdfplumber_recovery_exception" no longer emitted
No corpus paper's output changes; the change bites only outside the corpus.

highlights.message: Convert Grobid TEI to bibr export schema 12.0
highlights.body:
grobid_to_bibr(schema_version = "12.0") converts Grobid TEI into a 12.x
paper and saves it as a 12.0 file:

- ids are 1-based positions in document order;
- xref targets come from the xml:id each <ref> points at, for bib,
  figure, table and foot references;
- each caption and footnote is one text row with no section, after the
  body and the reference list, and there are no pseudo-sections; a
  caption starts with its printed label, taken from <head> when figDesc
  leaves it out;
- the source is the PDF next to the TEI (published.pdf for
  published.pdf.tei.xml), else the TEI, so source.sha256 matches a bibr
  export of the same PDF; paper_id is the source's name without its
  extension;
- the producer is Grobid, with the version in the TEI header, and the
  converter is metacheck; completed_at is when Grobid extracted the
  content, from the same header, else the time of the conversion;
- metacheck's own warning codes start with METACHECK_.

The body sentences are made as before. Without schema_version, the
conversion is unchanged.
highlights.author: Jakub Werner

highlights.message: Write bibr export schema 12.0 with paper_write()
highlights.body:
paper_write(schema_version = "12.0") saves a paper read from a bibr 12.0
export as a 12.0 file. It keeps the paper's extraction block, so a bibr
export keeps bibr as its producer and bibr's completed_at, and names
metacheck as the converter: rewriting bibr's exports changes nothing but
converter. bib_match rows made by add_bib_match() are converted to the
12.0 columns, and a score that is not on the 0-1 scale is written as null
with a METACHECK_MATCH_SCORE_NOT_0_1 warning. A paper in the older format
is refused, and so is one read from a later 12.x, since its rewrite would
have to keep keys metacheck does not know. Without schema_version,
paper_write() writes what it wrote before.

The tests validate what they write against bibr's strict schema (a copy
in tests/testthat/fixtures/bibr12) when jsonvalidate, now in Suggests, is
installed.
highlights.author: Jakub Werner

highlights.message: Read bibr export schema 12.x files
highlights.body:
.read_bibr() now sends a file with a root schema_version (bibr export
schema 11 and later) to .read_bibr12(), which reads 12.x and stops on any
other version. Files without a root schema_version read exactly as
before. Keys that a later 12.x adds are ignored.

A 12.x paper keeps metacheck's info table, made from metadata and source,
and info_match (metadata_match); the other tables keep their 12.x names
and meanings. Captions and footnotes are text rows with no section that
figure, table and the new footnote table point at with text_id; xref_id
is the row's own key and target_id the row it cites; paper$extraction
holds the export's extraction block. Degrees of freedom stay in
parentheses, as metacheck's statistics code expects.

inst/schema/paper-bibr12.json lists the optional tables and columns this
adds. paper_validate() and .paper_coerce() merge it into paper.json and
skip properties that are not tables (extraction); paper() and paper.json
are unchanged. ref_consistency, ref_miscitation and the table captions of
match_reported_output() read 12.x papers, and ref_accuracy compares the
0-1 match scores of 12.x papers with suggest_score / 100.
